name: Dreamer Development
description: Two modules that change how you read and work a patch rather than how it sounds, and that apply to every module in the rack, whoever wrote it. Clarity draws every port and cable so a patch can be read at a glance: colour for the kind of signal, a ring for input or output, cables that show which way the signal is flowing, one cable traced through a tangle, pinch to zoom, and cables picked up with a click rather than a drag. Test Gear takes no rack space at all. Right-click any port and clip something onto it: a gate button, a trigger, a clock, a DC level, an LFO, a VCO, a note or volt-per-octave source, noise, an attenuverter — and they work on a port that already has a cable in it — or an oscilloscope, a frequency analyser that reads the peak as a note, or an audio monitor for listening to that point. Everything you attach is saved with the patch. Every feature is a switch on the panel, so what it does is what you can see.

modules.name: Clarity
modules.description: User interface clarity: a patch you can read at a glance. Every port tells you what it is without reading the panel — colour for the kind of signal, and a ring that says input or output, the same on every module, whoever wrote it. Cables take the colour of where they go, with dashes crawling along them, so there is never a moment wondering which way a signal is flowing. Trace one cable through a tangle, pinch to zoom, and pick cables up with a click. Each of these is a switch on the panel, so what it does is what you can see.

modules.name: Test Gear
modules.description: Test gear for your rack. Right-click any port and clip an instrument onto it: an oscilloscope, a frequency analyser that reads the peak as a note, or an audio monitor that lets you listen to that point through one output port. There are sources too — gate, pulse, clock, DC, LFO, VCO, note, volt per octave, noise and an attenuverter — and they work on a port that already has a cable in it. Everything you attach is saved with the patch.
